title: altered cognitive processes shape tactile perception in autism
author: ourania semelidou
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0

steps.title: House and maintain mice
steps.instruction: Keep second‑generation Fmr1 knockout (Fmr1‑/y) and wild‑type littermate mice (5–16 weeks old) on a C57Bl/6 J background in a conventional facility at 22–24 °C, 40–60 % humidity, 12 h/12 h light‑dark cycle (lights on at 21:00). Provide ad libitum food and water until the water‑restriction period; house mice in collective cages (2–4 males per cage) with cotton nestlets and carton tubes, balancing genotypes per cage.

steps.title: Implement water‑restriction protocol
steps.instruction: From day 3 of habituation, give mice access to liquid water only in the experimental setup and a solid water supplement (Hydrogel, BioServices) in the home cage. Provide 1.5–2 ml water per day (≈50–65 % of ad libitum intake) to keep body weight loss ≤10 %. Supply 6–8 g Hydrogel per mouse each weekend. Record daily body weight and adjust supplemental water as needed.

steps.title: Habituate mice to handling and head‑fixation
steps.instruction: Handle mice (P40‑P50) using carton tubes and the cupping technique until they eat while being handled. Gradually habituate them to the head‑fixation tube for 5 days, increasing duration each day. On day 3 begin the water‑restriction protocol described above.

steps.title: Assemble vibrotactile decision‑making setup
steps.instruction: Place the setup in an isolation cubicle under red light. Head‑fix the mouse in a body tube with forepaws on two 6 mm steel bars (Thorlabs). Mount a Preloaded Piezo Actuator (P‑841.6, Physik Instrumente) with strain‑gauge feedback on the right bar, controlled by E‑501 (Physik Instrumente) in closed loop. Attach a 12.7 mm stainless‑steel post vertically to the actuator and clamp a 0.6 mm horizontal stainless‑steel rod (contact bar) onto it. Install two 20G (1.9 mm tip) metal feeding needles left and right of the mouth, each connected to a Sanworks solenoid‑valve lickport with capacitive sensor (Bpod_CapacitivePortInterface). Control the entire system with Bpod (Sanworks) via Python scripts (PyBpod).

steps.title: Define vibrotactile stimuli
steps.instruction: Generate sinusoidal vibrations at 40 Hz, 500 ms duration. Use two amplitudes: 12 µm peak‑to‑peak (low salience) and 26 µm peak‑to‑peak (high salience). For testing also use 20, 22, 24, 26 µm (high) and 12, 14, 16, 18 µm (low). Deliver 8 µl water reward at the lickport corresponding to stimulus salience (right for high, left for low).

steps.title: Train mice – automatic water phase
steps.instruction: Run sessions of 200–300 trials with a 1:1 ratio of high‑ and low‑salience stimuli. Each trial: deliver stimulus, then a 2 s response window. At the start of the response window automatically dispense 8 µl water at the lickport matching stimulus salience (left for 12 µm, right for 26 µm). Inter‑trial interval 5–10 s.

steps.title: Train mice – block training phase
steps.instruction: Present blocks of 20 consecutive trials of the same stimulus amplitude (either 12 µm or 26 µm). Lick the correct port to trigger water delivery; licking the wrong port triggers a 5 s timeout. Continue until mice achieve ≥70 % correct and ≤30 % incorrect choices for both amplitudes.

steps.title: Train mice – pseudorandom phase
steps.instruction: Present high‑ and low‑salience trials in pseudorandom order (maintaining a 1:1 overall ratio). Lick the correct port to receive water; incorrect licks cause a 5 s timeout. Adjust the high/low ratio if a mouse shows a consistent bias. Criterion: >70 % correct and <30 % incorrect choices on average for three consecutive days.

steps.title: Test mice on discrimination task
steps.instruction: Run sessions with pseudorandom delivery of amplitudes ranging from 12 µm to 26 µm (20, 22, 24, 26 µm rewarded right; 12, 14, 16, 18 µm rewarded left). Include only sessions where mice previously achieved >70 % correct on the training stimuli (12 µm and 26 µm). Record lick responses during the 2 s response window; miss trials are those with no lick.

steps.title: Analyze behavioral data
steps.instruction: Use custom Python scripts to compute for each stimulus salience: (1) Correct choice rate = correct licks / total trials, (2) Incorrect choice rate = wrong licks / total trials, (3) Missed stimulus rate = no‑lick trials / total trials. Exclude epochs where the animal disengaged. Calculate training duration as total days spent in block and pseudorandom phases. For testing, fit psychometric curves to right‑ward lick rates using a general linear model (≈84 repetitions per amplitude). Compute sensitivity d′ = z(lick right | high) – z(lick right | low). Compute criterion c = –½ [ z(lick right | high) + z(lick right | low) ]. Determine categorization bias as the logistic curve midpoint (μ) and precision as the slope. Calculate prior‑choice impact separately for low‑ and high‑salience trials as (correct + incorrect of current salience) / (all correct + all incorrect).
